So xgl was originally developed by a Novell employee back in 2006. It was made to allow hardware acceleration of X through opengl drivers. With a composite manager built on top of it(compiz/beryl) there were a ton of cool effects you could do with your desktop. It was absolutely revolutionary at the time, the open source forums were littered with tutorials/pics/videos. But the nostalgia eventually died out. Xgl was replaced by AIGLX, which was developed by a redhat employee. Basically AIGLX is the same as XGL, but solves the problem of allowing opengl to be used by a composite window manager in a different way, so that it can run alongside the X server as an extension. This caused X to remove XGL in favor of AIGLX. You can still get all these effects today if you really want.
